clue.text: Become too enthusiastic in the sea

definitions.meaning: to get carried away and overdo something, as an idiom
literally fallen over the side of a ship into the water

explanation.surface: Someone gets carried away with excitement while out on the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for overdoing one's enthusiasm, and literally having dropped from a ship into the water.

clue.text: A gneiss cut away could be a specific geological feature

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Some metamorphic rock hacked off might be a notable landform.
explanation.walkthrough: The Giant's Causeway is a basalt column formation on the coast of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The basalt column formation in County Antrim is a famous individual geological site.

clue.text: Nobody arrives on time for piece to be performed

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits on top of the next

parts.note: none means not one person

explanation.surface: No one turns up punctually for the concert item.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition written for nine players or singers.

clue.text: It should make births etc so uncomplicated, not hard

definitions.text: It should make births etc so uncomplicated, not hard

indicators.note: the letters are untangled into a fresh order once hard is removed

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A medical speciality aims to make childbirth simple and easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from the letters of BIRTHS ETC SO before 'uncomplicated' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical speciality dealing with childbirth aims to make deliveries go smoothly.

clue.text: Intellectual leader pursuing urge

indicators.note: the leader word follows the urge word

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A clever ringleader goes after a strong desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is informal for a highbrow or brainy person.

clue.text: Having support, succeeded stopping one escaping

indicators.note: succeeded's letter plugs the middle of the escaper word

parts.note: a bolter is a person or horse that bolts
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: With backing, a successor halts a fugitive.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, as a long pillow supports.

clue.text: Host extremely foolish to lose head

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the word for crazy

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A party-giver acts like a complete idiot and loses their cool.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, such as an armed force.

clue.text: Notice poor cloth, mostly bare, being picked up for garment

indicators.note: in a down clue the run of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to notice is to see
a rag is a scrap of shabby cloth

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: nude means bare

explanation.surface: Spotting shabby fabric, nearly naked, lifted up for clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE + RAG + NUD (NUDE missing its E) runs SEERAGNUD, which reads upwards as DUNGAREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls or trousers with a bib, an item of clothing.

clue.text: One may be organising rites and preaching

definitions.text: One may be organising rites and preaching

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleric arranges the service and delivers a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cleric in charge of a parish leads services and preaches sermons.

clue.text: High priest left out of historical documents

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for the records

parts.note: annals are year-by-year historical records

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's name is missing from the old records.
explanation.walkthrough: Annas is the high priest before whom Jesus was first brought in John's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Annas was the Jewish high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas, in the New Testament.

clue.text: Worker with prospects hoping to get rich?

definitions.text: Worker with prospects hoping to get rich?

parts.words: Worker with prospects hoping to get rich
parts.note: prospects reads as career hopes, but means sites being prospected for precious metal by a digger

explanation.surface: An ambitious employee dreams of wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector digging for precious ore literally works prospects in hope of a fortune.

clue.text: Like terrible fight when little kid meets boy in barren area

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the boy's name is placed inside the word for open wasteland

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
Ed is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A toddler encounters a lad out on the moor, leading to a fierce fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight to the death is the most desperate kind, continued until one party dies.

clue.text: Foul voice coming over the radio

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: bass is the lowest male singing voice

explanation.surface: A rough-sounding singer is heard on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low, mean or vile in character, the same as foul.

clue.text: Period on computer for Vicar of Bray

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: a time is a period
a server is a computer serving a network

explanation.surface: A clergyman spends a session on the PC.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray, from an English song, kept his post by switching faith with each monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's vicar is the classic turncoat who changes principles to suit those in power.

clue.text: Danced with toreador's equipment?

parts.note: a bullfighter's cape
the cape a bullfighter waves is traditionally red

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's gear prompts a lively jig.
explanation.walkthrough: The toreador's kit is read as a red cape, giving CAPE then RED; 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap about playfully, so capered is a past-tense synonym for danced.

clue.text: Publication has a page put in for each sponsor

parts.note: per means for each
to back is to sponsor

explanation.surface: A magazine includes an extra page for every backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' just sets the page and 'a' in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a book with soft covers, a kind of published work.

clue.text: Something put on train that payment covers

indicators.note: the payment word goes around the train word, covering it

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: An item loaded on a railway train is covered by the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests the railway; here it is the verb, as in training a gun on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is clothing, which is something one puts on.

clue.text: After time away, gets to the bottom of a case

definitions.text: After time away, gets to the bottom of a case

parts.words: After time away, gets to the bottom of a case
parts.note: reads like a detective solving a mystery after a break, but describes emptying a suitcase on returning from holiday

explanation.surface: Back from leave, a detective cracks a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptying luggage after a trip means removing everything down to its base.

clue.text: Excessively deferential society initially undermined by liberal

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter sits above the generous word
the first letter of society

parts.note: lavish means generous or liberal in giving

explanation.surface: Fawning high society is subverted by a progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish means servile, abjectly submissive like a slave.

clue.text: Rock is obstructing part of course

indicators.note: the word is stands in the middle of the course feature, blocking it

parts.note: a green is the putting surface on a golf course

explanation.surface: A boulder blocks part of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Greisen is a granite-derived rock made of quartz and mica.

clue.text: Old vessels left out to collect black lumps of food?

indicators.note: the shortened vessel word gathers black inside
the letter for left is removed

parts.note: goblets are old-style drinking cups
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Antique cups are left out to gather dark bits of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbets are chunks or morsels, especially of food.

clue.text: Bring in vessel in the sound

indicators.note: the vessel word is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A pot is brought ashore in a coastal strait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' could be a stretch of sea; it signals pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to bring it in as income.

clue.text: Capital's landmark appears as blur in parade

indicators.note: the word for blur goes inside the word for parade

parts.note: a march is a procession
to blear is to blur or dim

explanation.surface: A London monument looks fuzzy amid a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR + BLEAR + CH. MARBLE ARCH is a triumphal arch at the end of Oxford Street in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This white triumphal arch is a well-known London landmark near Hyde Park.

clue.text: Uplifted? Not one that's totally devastated

indicators.note: the word for one is not present

parts.note: raised means lifted up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Feeling uplifted? Not someone who is completely wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rased is a spelling of razed, meaning levelled to the ground.

clue.text: Small female mouse heard

indicators.note: the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Minnie Mouse is the Disney cartoon heroine

explanation.surface: A little rodent is heard squeaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini means very small, as in a miniature version.

clue.text: Killer of mite given a caution — one detectives held

indicators.note: one and the detectives are held inside the word for caution

parts.note: care means caution
I is the Roman numeral one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A pest-killer is issued a police caution while detectives hold someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An acaricide is a pesticide that kills mites and ticks.

clue.text: Screen guest but without modern technology

indicators.note: the guest word loses the letters for technology

parts.note: a visitor is a guest
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A visitor is shown the TV set, yet has no gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a shade or shield that screens the eyes or face.

clue.text: Men given a game somewhere in London

parts.note: knights are chessmen, pieces in chess
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Some chaps are handed a game somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHTSBRIDGE is an upmarket district of London, home of Harrods.
explanation.definitionFit: Knightsbridge is a fashionable district of central London.
